<section_guide number="4" title="Non-Functional Requirements" references="1,2,3">
<purpose>Propose the quality expectations the user or business can observe, each with a threshold or yes/no condition.</purpose>

<questions>
1. Ask only when a protected quality decision or a missing threshold cannot be safely proposed: which expectation should the product guarantee?
</questions>

<workflow>
Read Sections 1-3. Propose every quality expectation the requirements imply: responsiveness as
users experience it, availability when the business needs it, privacy, data location, access
isolation, accessibility, auditability, and similar expectations.

Define each as `NFR-n` at the start of a table row or list item, with threshold, unit, population
and observation condition; scope (`Global` or FR IDs); Required or Optional; and basis. When a
number is unsuitable, state a yes/no condition. Keep every security, privacy, regulatory,
accessibility, and contractual condition; Lite has no NFR count limit. Never invent a threshold the
user did not supply or approve — propose it as a candidate in the digest. Stay at the
business-observable level; never specify infrastructure metrics or technology.

When no quality expectation applies, record that in one sentence.
</workflow>

<completion required="true">Confirm every NFR with its threshold or condition, scope, and required flag before saving 4.1.</completion>
</section_guide>
